# Video Converter

- Route: `/tools/video-converter`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `video`
- Slug: `video-converter`

## Summary

Convert between MP4, WebM, MOV, AVI, MKV, and more — with full control over codecs, resolution, and audio. (Video tools)

## Details

Different platforms want different video formats. Edit on a Mac in MOV, post to the web in MP4 or WebM, archive in MKV. Media Manipulator handles every common video container and codec in one place, with full control over bitrate, resolution, and audio.
### What it does
- Converts between MP4, WebM, MOV, AVI, MKV, FLV, WMV, and ProRes.
- Choose codec (H.264, H.265, VP9, ProRes, DNxHD).
- Resize, change frame rate, trim, and re-encode audio.
- Apply filters and color grading optionally.
### How to use it
1. Upload video: Drop in any common video container.
2. Pick target format: MP4, WebM, MOV, AVI, MKV.
3. Tune codec and quality: Bitrate, resolution, audio.
4. Download: Save the converted video.
### Technical details
- H.264 in MP4 is the safe-everywhere default.
- H.265 (HEVC) and VP9 give ~25–50% smaller files at the same visual quality, but need a modern player.
- For editing handoffs, ProRes (in MOV) or DNxHD (in MOV/MXF) preserve the most quality.
### Use cases
- MOV → MP4: Make Apple-shot footage playable everywhere.
- AVI → MP4: Modernize an old archive video.
- MP4 → WebM: Shrink web video for modern browsers.
- Editor handoffs: Export ProRes or DNxHD for high-quality editing.
### FAQ
Q: What output format is best?
A: MP4 with H.264 for compatibility, WebM with VP9 for the smallest web files.
Q: Can I trim before converting?
A: Yes — the trim section of the form lets you cut the clip down before re-encoding.
Q: Will my audio stay in sync?
A: Yes — FFmpeg keeps A/V sync. If you change frame rate or speed, audio is resampled accordingly.
Q: Is there a file-size limit?
A: Very large files may be rejected on the free tier. Try lowering the resolution first.
